message.content:
There are \(2008\) integers from \(0\) to \(2007\), inclusive. Since \(2008\) is even and the range starts at \(0\), exactly half are even and half are odd:

\[
P(\text{even})=\frac{1004}{2008}=\frac12,\qquad P(\text{odd})=\frac12.
\]

We need \(ad-bc\) to be even, which is equivalent to

\[
ad \equiv bc \pmod 2.
\]

The parity of \(ad\) is odd only if both \(a\) and \(d\) are odd. Thus

\[
P(ad \text{ odd})=\frac12\cdot \frac12=\frac14,
\]
so
\[
P(ad \text{ even})=\frac34.
\]

The same is true for \(bc\). Since the pairs \((a,d)\) and \((b,c)\) are independent, \(ad\) and \(bc\) are independent. Therefore,

\[
P(ad-bc \text{ even})
= P(ad \text{ and } bc \text{ have the same parity})
\]

\[
= P(\text{both odd})+P(\text{both even})
= \left(\frac14\right)^2+\left(\frac34\right)^2
= \frac{1}{16}+\frac{9}{16}
= \frac{10}{16}
= \frac58.
\]

The answer is \(\boxed{\frac58}\).
